newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Electric to enter long-distance call market.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Electric to enter long-distance call market.

text.p: Japanese electric machinery maker Mitsubishi Electric Corp said on Tuesday that it would enter the domestic long-distance phone market next May to take advantage of recent telecoms deregulation.

A wholly owned subsidiary of the company, Mitsubishi Electric Information Network Corp, will offer long-distance calls in nine cities at rates more than 25 percent lower than existing services, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.

The government allowed companies which hold lines leased from long-distance carriers for their internal telecoms needs to offer public call services via those lines from October. The measure is expected to promote competition, especially in the long-distance market, and bring down prices.
Mitsubishi Electric will connect its leased line to the public phone network to provide the new service in the nine cities, which include Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, Sapporo and Hiroshima.
The government deregulation helps big firms with extensive leased-line networks to reduce their in-house communications costs by "re-leasing" the lines.
A spokesman for consumer electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said the company was considering launching a similar service.

However, industry officials have pointed out that the cut-throat price competition between the nation's three existing domestic carriers has already brought phone rates down so low that newcomers would be hard pressed to keep up.

In the latest round of the phone price war, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, Japan's biggest telecoms company, has pledged to cut its domestic long-distance rates to 100 yen (90 U.S. cents) per three minutes from the current 140 yen ($1.26) by 2000.
Mitsubishi Electric is involved in industrial machinery, data communications systems and consumer electronics.
